title: Week 2 of the AI business challenge: getting the first paying user
summary: Rob checks in on three beginners building AI products on a $100 budget over six weeks. The focus is the first dollar: one builder stalls on a $1 offer with no audience, while another converts her waitlist into five paying users. Mostly vlog and updates, with a few usable lessons on validation and consistency.

principles.text: The first milestone is a stranger paying you, not a free user or a friend.
principles.quote: Not a free user, not your friend, someone actually giving you your first dollar.

principles.text: A very low price doesn't guarantee an impulse buy; without an audience, even $1 gets no takers.
principles.quote: My assumption was if it's $1, it's an impulse buy. Um but apparently either not enough audience or I yeah.

principles.text: When a public offer gets silence, reach out directly to many people to learn why.
principles.quote: So, the challenge would be to try and reach out to 100 people somehow until until next week is over.

principles.text: A pre-launch waitlist can be converted into early paying users with a lifetime-access offer.
principles.quote: I sent an email to everyone who signed up to my wait list and some people actually were interested in paying like a small amount $5 to get a lifetime access to the app once it's live.

principles.text: Find a hook people believe in, and share your journey publicly to draw buyers.
principles.quote: thought what are the hooks that people would believe in that would make them pay that $1. So, I kind of just shared my journey and people came to me and were interested.

principles.text: Talent without consistency doesn't build anything.
principles.quote: But talent without consistency doesn't build anything.
